question: What’s happening here?
text:
The question is about Bilqis (the queen of Sheba) sending a gift. The books give this reason: she judged that a gift would work on people and might keep Sulayman from attacking, so she chose peace over fighting. She knew that Sulayman had no need for her armies and that she could not stand against his soldiers, so she said to them: I fear that if we fight him, he will come at us with his armies and destroy us. Her plan was to send him a gift befitting one of his status, and see what his response would be, perhaps he would accept it and leave us alone, or would impose a tribute on us that we would pay each year.

Ibn Kathir (English, abridged): 'I will send him a gift befitting for one of his status, and will wait and see what his response will be. She understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people."

Ibn Kathir (Arabic): Ibn 'Abbas and others said: she told her people that if he accepts the gift, he is a king, so fight him; but if he does not accept it, he is a Prophet, so follow him.

The books also differ on the wisdom of her choice: Qatada praised her, saying how intelligent she was in her Islam and in her disbelief! She knew that a gift would have an effect on people.

sources.quote: قَالَ الْحَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيُّ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: فَوَّضُوا أَمْرَهُمْ إِلَى عِلْجة تَضْطَرِبُ ثَدْيَاهَا، فَلَمَّا قَالُوا لَهَا مَا قَالُوا، كَانَتْ هِيَ أَحْزَمَ رَأْيًا مِنْهُمْ، وَأَعْلَمَ بِأَمْرِ سُلَيْمَانَ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا قِبَلَ لَهَا بِجُنُودِهِ وَجُيُوشِهِ، وَمَا سُخّر لَهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ وَالطَّيْرِ، وَقَدْ شاهَدَت مِنْ قَضِيَّةِ الْكِتَابِ مَعَ الْهُدْهُدِ أَمْرًا عَجِيبًا بَدِيعًا، فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ:
sources.before:
ا؛ وَلِهَذَا قَالَتْ: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلأ أَفْتُونِي فِي أَمْرِي مَا كُنْتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا حَتَّى تَشْهَدُونِ﴾ أَيْ: حَتَّى تَحْضُرُونَ وَتُشِيرُونَ.

﴿قَالُوا نَحْنُ أُولُو قُوَّةٍ وَأُولُو بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ أَيْ: مَنوا إِلَيْهَا بعَدَدهم وَعَدَدِهِمْ وَقُوَّتِهِمْ، ثُمَّ فَوَّضُوا إِلَيْهَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَ فَقَالُوا: ﴿وَالأمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَانْظُرِي مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ﴾ أَيْ: نَحْنُ لَيْسَ لَنَا عَاقَةٌ [وَلَا بِنَا بَأْسٌ، إِنْ شِئْتِ أَنْ تَقْصِدِيهِ وَتُحَارِبِيهِ، فَمَا لَنَا عَاقَةٌ] عَنْهُ. وَبَعْدَ هَذَا فَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ، مُرِي فِينَا بِرَأْيِكِ نَمْتَثِلُهُ وَنُطِيعُهُ.
sources.after:
إِنِّي أَخْشَى أَنْ نُحَارِبَهُ وَنَمْتَنِعَ عَلَيْهِ، فَيَقْصِدَنَا بِجُنُودِهِ، وَيُهْلِكَنَا بِمَنْ مَعَهُ، وَيَخْلُصَ إِلَيَّ وَإِلَيْكُمُ الْهَلَاكُ وَالدَّمَارُ دُونَ غَيْرِنَا؛ وَلِهَذَا قَالَتْ: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا﴾ .

قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: أَيْ إِذَا دَخَلُوا بَلَدًا عنْوَة أَفْسَدُوهُ، أَيْ: خَرّبوه، ﴿وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً﴾ أَيْ: وَقَصَدُوا مَنْ فِيهَا مِنَ الْوُلَاةِ وَالْجُنُودِ، فَأَهَانُوهُمْ غَايَةَ الْهَوَانِ، إِمَّا بِالْقَتْلِ أَوْ بِالْأَسْرِ.

قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: قَالَتْ بِلْقِيسُ: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَر
sources.said: She knew that Sulayman had no need for her armies and that she could not stand against his soldiers, so she said to them: I fear that if we fight him, he will come at us with his armies and destroy us.

sources.quote: meaning, 'I will send him a gift befitting for one of his status, and will wait and see what his response will be.
sources.before:
fit and we will obey. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Bilqis said:

إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَا أَذِلَّةً ۖ

(Verily, kings, when they enter a town, they destroy it and make the most honorable amongst its people the lowest.) And Allah said:

وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ

(And thus they do.) Then she resorted to peaceful means, seeking a truce and trying to placate Sulayman, and said:

وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ فَنَاظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ

(But verily, I am going to send him a present, and see with what the messengers return.)
sources.after: Perhaps he will accept that and leave us alone, or he will impose a tax which we can pay him every year, so that he will not fight us and wage war against us.' Qatadah said: "May Allah have mercy on her and be pleased with her – how wise she was as a Muslim and (before that) as an idolator! She understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people." Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "She said to her people, if he accepts the gift, he is a king, so fight him; but if he does not accept it, he is a Prophet, so follow him."
sources.said: 'I will send him a gift befitting for one of his status, and will wait and see what his response will be. She understood how gift-giving has a good effect on people.
